result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.rescale_layout()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Center and resize a layout that's already been computed. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.rescale_layout()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Center and resize a layout that's already been computed. title: >- [Graph.rescale_layout()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Center and resize a layout that's already been computed. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Center and resize a layout that's already been computed. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6336-L6419){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.rescale_layout( scale=1.0, center=(0.0, 0.0), pos="pos", attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Rescale a layout](../assets/graphs/rescale-layout.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A four-node cycle placed by hand: nodes 1 to 4 at (0, 0), (4, 8), (12, 8) and (16, 0), with a small cross at their mean (8, 4). After rescale_layout() the same shape is centered on the origin and fits the dashed square from -1 to 1: the nodes move to (-1, -0.5), (-0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5) and (1, -0.5), shown in accent." width="100%"} Shifts the positions so their mean sits at `center=`, then scales them evenly (keeping the drawing's shape) so the coordinate farthest from it is `scale=` away along `x` or `y`. Every `layout_*()` method does this to its own result; use this to bring positions from elsewhere (a file, another library, hand placement, or a layout run with `scale=None`) into the same frame, for example to draw two layouts side by side. With a single node, or all nodes at one point, the positions are only moved. Matches NetworkX's `rescale_layout_dict()` (and `rescale_layout()` on an array of positions) with the result shifted to `center=`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The largest distance from `center=` along either axis. Default is `1.0`. [center]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[float, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [(0.0, 0.0)]{.doc-parameter-default} : Where the positions' mean goes, as `(x, y)`. Default is the origin. [pos]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[str, dict]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["pos"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The positions to rescale: the name of a node attribute holding `(x, y)` pairs (default `"pos"`, where the `layout_*()` methods store them) or a `{node: (x, y)}` dictionary keyed by node ID or label. Only the nodes that have a position are rescaled. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the new positions in. If `None` (default), the attribute named by `pos=` (so it's rescaled in place), or `"pos"` when `pos=` is a dictionary. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the positions on the nodes and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, tuple[float, float]], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to `(x, y)` tuples. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `scale=` is not a positive number, `center=` is not a pair of numbers, no node has the `pos=` attribute, or a position is not a pair of finite numbers. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Positions placed by hand are centered on the origin and fit into the unit square: ::: {#bdc4f614 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(3) graph.rescale_layout(pos={1: (0, 0), 2: (10, 5), 3: (20, 10)}, return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: (-1.0, -0.5), 2: (0.0, 0.0), 3: (1.0, 0.5)} ``` ::: ::: Positions stored in a node attribute are rescaled in place: ::: {#0068defc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.set_node_attrs("xy", {1: [0, 0], 2: [6, 0], 3: [6, 3]}) graph.rescale_layout(scale=2, pos="xy").get_node_attrs("xy") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {2: [1.0, -0.5], 3: [1.0, 1.0], 1: [-2.0, -0.5]} ``` ::: :::
